newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian coconut oil extends losses, copra down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian coconut oil extends losses, copra down.

text.p: Indonesian coconut oil prices extended losses on Thursday on continued poor consumer demand while copra prices were down on ample supply, traders said.
They said coconut oil was quoted at 1,820-30 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 1,860 rupiah/kg a week ago and copra softened to 800 rupiah/kg from 850 rupiah/kg.

"Consumer demand is very poor and most players seem to be out of the market. I think refineries already have enough stock and they don't want to produce much when consumer demand is still low," said a Jakarta-based trader.
He said Manila's bearish trend also affected local sentiment.

Traders in Manila said on Monday coconut oil prices were seen steady in sluggish trade this week due to the Easter holidays. Indonesia is the world's second largest coconut producer after the Philippines and local traders often look to Manila for price direction.
One trader said copra prices continued to fall because supply was abundant in Indonesia.
"It's no use for producers to purchase copra when oil prices are low. They only use the existing stock to produce copra into oil and not more than that," she said.
"We have offered copra to producers and they have refused to buy. Maybe they think it's much better for them to keep their money in the bank than build stocks," said the trader.
Traders said they did not expect market sentiment to improve this week due to the absence of fresh factors. The market will be closed on Friday for Easter.
